# Exclusive-volume promotion and collision audit

Let U_1,...,U_k be the strict equal-mass cap cover constructed in
candidate b25c81940a686cf0, with closed cap masses tau M, where M=H_d(S).
Let E_i be the set of points of S belonging to U_i and no other open cap.
Write E=sum_i H_d(E_i). Except for hyperplane boundaries of zero relevant
measure, multiplicity counting gives

  k tau M >= E+2(M-E)=2M-E.                          (1)

In d=2, k<=3m, m=2^n, and tau<4/(9m) imply E>2M/3.

## All-pair promotion is globally disjoint

Choose one compact convex positive-volume piece A_i subset E_i in a fiber
z_i for each of some cap indices, requiring that coordinates within each
parity class be pairwise distinct. (This also makes all selected coordinates
globally distinct.) For every pair of selected indices whose coordinates
have the same parity, put B_ij=(A_i+A_j)/2.

Every B_ij lies in S and is covered only by caps i,j. All the B_ij are
pairwise disjoint and are disjoint from all the selected A_l:

* Pairs with different output integer coordinates are disjoint by definition.
* Pairs with disjoint cap-index sets cannot intersect: an intersection point
  would be outside every cap, contradicting the open cover.
* Two different pairs sharing cap i could have the same output coordinate
  only if their other endpoint coordinates were equal, which is excluded.
* B_ij cannot meet A_l for l outside {i,j}, by the disjoint cap-index argument;
  it cannot meet A_i or A_j because its midpoint coordinate differs from both.

Consequently the stronger global bound is

  M >= sum_i V_i + sum_{i<j:z_i congruent z_j mod 2}
                    ((V_i^(1/d)+V_j^(1/d))/2)^d,    (2)

where V_i=H_d(A_i). The right side is also at most k tau M, but (2) is
stronger when k tau>1. The disjointness remains valid between different
parity groups, since those pairs have disjoint cap-index sets.

## At most d+1 exclusive cap colors occur in any fiber

This holds for the full exclusive regions, not only preselected witnesses.
If d+2 distinct E_i meet one fiber, choose a point in each. Radon's theorem
partitions these points into two groups whose convex hulls intersect. The
common point is in the same S-fiber. For each cap, one of the groups consists
entirely of points outside that cap; their convex hull is therefore outside
its open interior. This gives a point outside every open cap, a contradiction.
Thus any integer fiber supports at most d+1 nonempty exclusive cap regions.

## A resolved restricted case: each exclusive color has one distinct fiber

Assume every E_i is supported in a single integer fiber z_i, and these
coordinates are pairwise distinct. Then

  E <= m tau M,  where m=2^n.                       (3)

Proof. Fix a parity class of cap indices and choose i with maximal exclusive
volume V_i=H_d(E_i). For every other j in that class, B_ij=(E_i+E_j)/2 is
covered only by i,j. Because it lies in a different integer fiber from both
endpoints, it cannot be exclusive to either one under the one-fiber
assumption. Hence it belongs to BOTH caps. These midpoint sets are pairwise
disjoint and disjoint from E_i. Brunn-Minkowski gives

  H_d(B_ij) >= ((V_i^(1/d)+V_j^(1/d))/2)^d >= V_j.

The mass of cap i is therefore at least the total exclusive volume of its
parity class. Sum over at most m parity classes to obtain (3). One may apply
the argument to compact convex approximations of the exclusive fibers and
pass to their volumes; all boundaries have zero relevant measure.

Combining (1), (3), and k<=m(d+1) yields

  tau >= 2/[m(d+2)].

For d=2 this is 1/(2m), strictly larger than the hypothesized 4/(9m), giving
a contradiction. Thus any genuine d=2 strict counterexample certificate
must have either multiple exclusive cap colors sharing a fiber or at least
one exclusive color carrying positive volume in several integer fibers.
The estimate alone does not extend to all d: at d=3, 2/(d+2)=2/5 is smaller
than gamma_3=27/64.

## A caution against a local multiplicity shortcut

The assertion that three planar caps each taking less than half of a convex
body must have total exclusive area at most two-thirds is false when their
masses are unequal. An exact example is

  K=conv{(-4,-2),(7,-2),(-2,3)}, area(K)=55/2,
  U_1={x>-1/100}, U_2={y>-1/100},
  U_3={x+y<1/100}.

These open halfplanes cover the entire plane. Their normalized closed-cap
areas are respectively

  491401/990000, 90601/250000, 361201/770000,

all strictly below 1/2. Their sum is 230051893/173250000 < 4/3.
Their total normalized exclusive area is

  58225471/86625000 > 2/3,

and exceeds half the sum of their cap areas by

  949997/115500000 > 0.

Thus a proof cannot apply E_z<=2M_z/3 or E_z<=L_z/2 fiberwise merely from a
local cap-mass bound of one half. Global equal cap masses do not give equal
cap masses inside individual fibers. This example is an auxiliary counter-
model; it is not a counterexample to OC or to the strict global cap threshold.
